A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MANGO work. The main text, equations, eight tables, seven figures and Appendices A–B are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MANGO evaluations on RGB-D segmentation, Taskonomy image translation and MM-IMDB classification, together with main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the additional ablations, computational-cost comparison and attention visualization in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The ICA layer, MMCA/IMCA/LICA partitioning, latent encoder and flow architecture, and joint likelihood/task objective remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NYUDv2 and SUN RGB-D segmentation, the same five Taskonomy translation scenarios and MM-IMDB classification. Newly mentioned scene-graph and brain-understanding applications are background examples, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 8 and the qualitative comparisons. This includes TokenFusion, GeminiFusion, the classification baselines and the Coupling Layer/Glow/Flow++/AttnFlow comparison; citation renumbering does not change the methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same dataset splits, 256 × 256 inputs, encoders, task heads and training settings. Evaluation metrics and the model configurations in the main and appendix experiments also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A retain the same analyses of invertible layers, partitioning, latent compression and block depth, including the 16-block experiment. Computational-cost analysis and attention visualization are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without explicit repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries and qualitative figures match. Examples include MANGO's 59.2/54.1 segmentation mIoU in Table 1, 71.7/68.2 micro/macro F1 in Table 3, and the appendix's 61.7/55.6 mIoU for 16 blocks in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the ICA invertibility and Jacobian-determinant reasoning, and the LU parameterization remain unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about explicit, interpretable and tractable fusion, ICA and its three partitioning mechanisms, latent-space scalability and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning cross-modal correlations, latent compression and depth/computation tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning objective balancing, computational constraints and untested larger-scale generalization.

D1.justification: The first-page hyperlink changes from the laboratory homepage to a MANGO-specific project page. New acknowledgments identify the GPU facility; the four-A100 setup and implementation settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: v2 adds ten references, expanding the introductory examples to scene-graph generation and human-brain understanding, among other areas. All earlier references are retained, and the substantive positioning against implicit fusion and prior flow methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 modestly expands the opening paragraph, updates affiliations and the conference footer, corrects the LLaMA spelling, and adds acknowledgments and an Appendices heading. The main section organization and technical exposition remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: The same seven figure images and eight table structures are retained, with local reflow and appendix repositioning. A new layout defect appears on v2 page 6: Figure 4's final caption line overlaps the sentence following Equation (7), which is separately legible in v1.

improvement.justification: The project-specific link, acknowledgments and broader background citations provide modest documentation benefits, while the scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. However, the new overlap between Figure 4's caption and the method text on page 6 directly reduces legibility. This localized presentation regression slightly outweighs the peripheral additions.
